title: AMD skill eval dataset
description: One dataset per skill at skills/<name>/evals/evals.json. Each case is a user prompt plus what should be true after the agent sees it. The same case is graded twice: routing mode installs the whole catalog and checks expect_skill, behavior mode installs only this skill and checks should / should_not / logs_contain / files_exist. Reference the schema from your file with "$schema": "../../../eval/schema/evals.schema.json" for editor autocomplete. eval/datasets.py is the enforcing implementation; this file exists so editors can help.

$schema.description: Points editors at this schema for autocomplete. Ignored by the runner.

_comment.description: Free-text notes for humans. Ignored by the runner.

cases.description: Tier 0 requires at least 3 cases that should trigger this skill and 2 that should not.

id.description: Stable slug, unique across the whole repo because routing pools every skill's cases into one run. Used by --only and to name transcript files.

prompt.description: What the user says, phrased the way a user would. Do not copy the skill description: that measures string matching rather than routing. A prompt that references a file must either stage it via `workspace` or link a real URL, because the routing workspace holds nothing but the skills tree.

expect_skill.description: Which skill must activate. OMIT for the normal case: it defaults to the skill that owns this file. Use null when no skill should fire (a near-miss for this skill). Use another skill's name to assert a handoff to a confusable neighbor.

should.description: Natural-language things the agent must do, graded by an LLM judge over the transcript and workspace. Not allowed on a case expecting no skill, where there is no skill to grade.

should_not.description: Natural-language things the agent must not do, graded by an LLM judge. This is where a skill's guard rails get pinned down.

logs_contain.description: Case-insensitive substrings that must appear in the run transcript. Deterministic and instant, so prefer these over a judged expectation when the thing you want is a literal (a script name, a flag, a pinned image tag). Do not assert the skill's own name here: routing mode already grades that.

files_exist.description: Workspace-relative paths that must exist as files when the run ends.

workspace.description: Directory relative to the skill root (conventionally evals/files/<name>) whose contents are copied into the agent's workspace before the prompt runs. Use it to hand the agent a starting file to edit instead of describing one in prose.

note.description: Why this case exists. JSON has no comments, so this is the sanctioned place for one. Ignored by the runner.
